summary_paragraph: A 65-year-old male with a complex history including end-stage renal disease on hemodialysis, coronary artery disease with prior CABG and stents, peripheral vascular disease, and type 2 diabetes was admitted for sudden-onset chest tightness associated with nausea and vomiting. The pain began at home and recurred during a dialysis session, prompting ER evaluation. Initial troponin levels were stable, and a nuclear stress test showed no reversible ischemia, indicating no acute coronary event. Management focused on optimizing anti-anginal therapy, including increasing metoprolol and switching from isosorbide dinitrate to once-daily isosorbide mononitrate. Fluid overload was noted on chest imaging and managed with dialysis. The patient also received podiatry care for chronic lower extremity ulcers. He remained stable, pain-free, and was discharged home with medication changes, weight monitoring instructions, and follow-up plans.
